submitted.rationale: Index 29 (In0.18Sb0.82) had the highest EQE of the three measured points, at 3.2e-4 %. The Sb-rich end may contain mixed-valence Sb6O13 (predicted gap 2.05 eV, below the 2.4 eV photon). All three EQE values are very low, so the whole In-Sb line looks close to inactive.

rejected.reason: In11Sb3O24 region (on hull, predicted gap 1.9 eV) measured EQE 9.6e-5 %, lower than index 29
InSbO4 composition (on hull, predicted gap 2.2 eV) measured a negative EQE of -6.6e-4 %, i.e. no photoactivity

consultations.verdict: Support: In11Sb3O24 (Sb 0.214) is on the MACE hull and MEGNet HSE gap 1.91 eV < 2.4 eV photon, so it absorbs; index 7 (Sb 0.204) is the closest candidate. InSbO4 (gap 2.2, stable) is the second target; In3Sb5O12 (2.77 eV) cannot absorb.

Support: InSbO4 (on hull) predicted gap about 2.2 eV (SCAN), below the 2.4 eV photon. Index 17 (Sb 0.508) is closest to the 1:1 stoichiometry. The In11Sb3O24 region gave very low EQE, so moving there.

Weak support: the mixed-valence Sb6O13 phase has a predicted HSE gap of 2.05 eV (<2.4 eV), so it can absorb, and the Sb-rich end has not been explored. The In2O3 gap of 2.2 eV is similar, but the In-rich side (index 7) was already near zero. The GP UCB also points to index 29.
